movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Edged up slightly last night. Analysts at HSBC flagged Microsoft as one of their top earnings picks, and separate commentary noted the stock looks attractively valued relative to its cash flow and AI growth story. Earnings are due next month — one to watch.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)

The GTA 6 news cycle continues — fans and analysts are watching for a gameplay trailer or pre-order announcement, with Take-Two's earnings call on August 7 expected to include first GTA 6 pre-order data. watch_today.title: TTWO: August 7 earnings call is a real catalyst — hold and watch
watch_today.detail: Take-Two's August 7 earnings call is confirmed to include the first GTA 6 pre-order data. That's a genuine market-moving event for a long-term holder. The stock dipped 1.2% last night — likely just noise ahead of the big reveal. Sit tight. If you're thinking of topping up, waiting to see the pre-order numbers first makes sense.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Earnings coming next month — analysts bullish, stock fairly valued
watch_today.detail: Multiple analysts including HSBC have flagged Microsoft as a top earnings pick. Commentary this week noted the stock looks cheap relative to earnings and its AI-driven cash flow growth. Still down 13% on your position overall, but the long-term thesis — cloud + AI dominance — remains fully intact. Hold and let the earnings catalyst do the work.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Small green day but still deep in the red — hold and be patient
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals ticked up 0.43% today and analysts are starting to write positively about it again as lithium demand gradually recovers. You're still down 31% on your position, which stings. But the long-term thesis — lithium is essential for the EV and battery transition — hasn't broken. Don't sell into weakness. Hold.

watch_today.title: RBA rate hike warning — watch impact on housing and bank stocks
watch_today.detail: At least one major Australian bank is now forecasting another RBA interest rate hike is imminent. If that happens, it would put further pressure on household budgets, house prices, and potentially Australian bank stocks. None of your direct holdings are Aussie bank stocks, but if you hold any property or are considering buying, this is worth watching closely this week.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX: Best mover today — AI tailwind intact, hold for the long run
watch_today.detail: Your AI ETF bounced 1.26% today, the strongest mover in the portfolio. Still down 10.9% overall on your cost base, but global AI momentum remains a strong structural tailwind. No news suggesting the thesis has changed — this is a long-term position and today's move is encouraging.

watch_today.title: Middle East tension — oil and gold to watch
watch_today.detail: US-Iran conflict is escalating with fresh missile strikes threatening a ceasefire and the Strait of Hormuz. The IEA has warned this could disrupt oil supply recovery. Oil dipped last night to $71.41 but could spike if the situation worsens. Gold also pulled back slightly. No direct impact on your holdings today, but worth watching if things escalate.

world.summary: Trump moves to reshape US election oversight, the US-Iran conflict escalates with missile strikes near the Strait of Hormuz, and Israel now controls nearly 70% of Gaza nine months into a ceasefire.

stories.title: Trump fires members of independent US election commission — accused of trying to 'rig' elections
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration fired members of the Election Assistance Commission — the independent federal body that helps states run elections and certify voting systems. Critics, including Democrats and some Republicans, have accused Trump of trying to 'rig' future elections by gutting oversight. On top of that, the administration announced it will tie states' anti-terrorism funding to compliance with federal election security directives, giving Washington more leverage over how individual states run their votes. It's a major shift in how US democracy is supervised — and it's stoking a fierce constitutional fight.

stories.title: US-Iran war escalates: missile strikes threaten Middle East ceasefire and global oil supply
stories.why_it_matters: Fresh missile strikes between the US and Iran are threatening to unravel a fragile ceasefire in the Middle East. The International Energy Agency (IEA) has specifically warned that the escalation threatens the recovery of global oil supply — the Strait of Hormuz, which sits between Iran and Oman, is one of the world's most critical shipping chokepoints, with roughly 20% of global oil passing through it. If it were blocked or disrupted, petrol prices worldwide — including in Australia — could spike sharply. Markets are watching this closely.

stories.title: Israel now controls nearly 70% of Gaza — nine months into a ceasefire
stories.why_it_matters: Despite a ceasefire being in place for nine months, NPR reports that Israel has steadily expanded its military control and now occupies close to 70% of Gaza's territory. This raises serious questions about what a post-war Gaza actually looks like — and whether the ceasefire is a genuine pause or a slow annexation. The humanitarian situation for Palestinians in the remaining areas is reported to be dire. It's a development that's drawing increasing international condemnation and complicating US diplomatic relationships in the region.

stories.title: Wimbledon 2026: Sinner vs Zverev set for men's final — Cruz Hewitt reaches junior final
stories.why_it_matters: World number one Jannik Sinner and Alexander Zverev have set up a blockbuster Wimbledon men's final — their 15th career meeting. Meanwhile, Cruz Hewitt — son of Australian legend Lleyton — has reached the Wimbledon junior final, 24 years after his dad won the men's title there. It's a feel-good Australian angle on a big week of tennis, though reports of ugly behind-the-scenes tensions between Lleyton and Cruz have also surfaced, adding an awkward family drama subplot to an otherwise great story.

politics.summary: Major Australian banks are warning another RBA interest rate hike could be imminent — a potential headache for mortgage holders and property investors heading into the second half of 2026.

stories.title: Major bank warns RBA rate hike is coming — and house prices could tank
stories.why_it_matters: At least one of Australia's big four banks is now publicly forecasting that the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) will raise interest rates again in the near future. If that happens, it would be another blow for the 1-in-3 Australian households with a mortgage — monthly repayments would rise again after a period of holding steady. The AFR is also reporting that higher rates could put downward pressure on house prices and bank stocks. For everyday Australians, the message is clear: if you've got a variable-rate mortgage, your repayments could soon go up again. For property investors, the outlook is increasingly uncomfortable.

ai.summary: This week's AI news is dominated by regulatory questions — from constitutional debates about AI laws in the US to New York using AI to cut government red tape. There's also a practical consumer deal worth knowing about.

stories.title: New York is using AI to slash government red tape — a real-world test of AI in bureaucracy
stories.why_it_matters: New York State has launched an AI-assisted regulatory overhaul — essentially using AI tools to scan thousands of pages of outdated government rules and flag which ones can be simplified or removed. The goal is to cut bureaucratic red tape that slows down businesses and individuals. It's one of the first large-scale uses of AI to actually streamline government, rather than just talk about it. If it works, expect other states and countries (potentially including Australian governments) to follow suit.

stories.title: One platform to rule them all: use GPT, Gemini, Claude and more simultaneously for a one-off $60
stories.why_it_matters: A new AI platform is getting attention this week — it lets you run ChatGPT (OpenAI), Gemini (Google), Claude (Anthropic) and other AI models side-by-side in one interface, so you can compare their answers or use the best tool for each job. It's being sold as a one-time $60 lifetime deal rather than multiple monthly subscriptions. Practically speaking, it's useful if you regularly use AI for writing, research, or work tasks and want access to the best models without paying separately for each.

stories.title: Is private AI regulation constitutional? A growing legal debate in the US
stories.why_it_matters: The Wall Street Journal ran an opinion piece this week asking whether laws regulating private AI companies might actually be unconstitutional in the US. This matters because it's a sign that the legal framework around AI regulation is still very much being argued from scratch — there's no settled playbook. For investors in AI stocks or ETFs (like your GXAI.AX), regulatory uncertainty cuts both ways: it could slow AI companies down, or it could mean they operate with less government interference for longer.

sport.summary: Big NRL Round 19 action underway — the Sharks obliterated the Dolphins 66-0 in a historic win, while the Warriors cruised past the Tigers. Wimbledon is heating up with Cruz Hewitt making the junior final and a Sinner vs Zverev men's final set for Sunday.

stories.title: Sharks smash Dolphins 66-0 — Nicho Hynes makes history at Kayo Stadium
stories.why_it_matters: The Cronulla Sharks absolutely demolished the Dolphins 66-0 at Kayo Stadium on Saturday afternoon — one of the biggest thrashings of the NRL season. Halfback Nicho Hynes reportedly made history with his performance. It's a catastrophic result for the Dolphins, who conceded 66 unanswered points at their home ground. The Sharks look genuine finals contenders.

stories.title: Warriors demolish Wests Tigers 32-6 — Tigers' finals hopes on life support
stories.why_it_matters: Friday night's game saw the Warriors run out comfortable 32-6 winners over Wests Tigers at Campbelltown. The Tigers' finals hopes are now described as 'paper thin' — and judiciary concerns loom for the club heading into next week. The Warriors continue to look strong and are firmly in the top-eight mix.

stories.title: Cruz Hewitt reaches Wimbledon junior final — 24 years after dad Lleyton's triumph
stories.why_it_matters: Cruz Hewitt — Lleyton's son — has made the Wimbledon junior boys final, 24 years after his father won the men's title on the same courts in 2002. It's a remarkable family story. However, the week has also been clouded by reports of tension between Lleyton and Cruz behind the scenes, with 'staggering scenes' reported at Wimbledon that have put an awkward spotlight on the father-son relationship. Cruz plays his final on the weekend.

stories.title: Wimbledon men's final: Sinner vs Zverev — their 15th career meeting
stories.why_it_matters: World number one Jannik Sinner and Alexander Zverev will face off in Sunday's Wimbledon men's final — their 15th career meeting, making it one of the most familiar rivalries in tennis. Sinner goes in as favourite. Australia's Sam Hewitt (Lleyton's nephew) is also reportedly on the cusp of breaking a 15-year Australian drought — Fox Sports reports an Aussie could be in contention in the tournament. A great weekend of tennis ahead.

stories.title: AFL Round 18 wrap: Bulldogs make six changes, Magpies forward set for absence
stories.why_it_matters: Heading into AFL Round 18 action this weekend: the Western Bulldogs have made six changes to their lineup — a big reshuffle that signals either injury trouble or a deliberate shake-up. A Collingwood forward is also set for a stint on the sidelines. Carlton made a significant change flagged by the club on Friday. The Dees (Melbourne) have also lost a key player. Plenty of team news to absorb before you lock in your tipping.
